_about: Curated one-line takeaways and key findings per body system for the atlas overview cards. Grades are read from the findings themselves.

vascular.takeaway: Circulation when upright is the most consistent abnormality: low blood volume, small stroke volume and a large fall in brain blood flow.
groups: Low red cell and total blood volume
Brain blood flow falls about 26% on tilt, vs 7%
Small heart volumes and stroke volume

muscle-exertion.takeaway: Exercise capacity is lower and recovery takes days; how much is a muscle defect rather than poor delivery is open.
groups: PEM starts hours to a day later and lasts days
Low cardiac filling and poor oxygen extraction
Worse on a second exercise test
Low mitochondrial function in blood cells
Patient serum impairs healthy muscle cells

neuro.takeaway: Brain blood flow, autonomic tone and cognition are measurably affected; brain imaging and inflammation markers are inconsistent.
groups: Brain blood flow falls on tilt
Higher heart rate, lower heart-rate variability
Nerve injury markers in blood or CSF

immune.takeaway: Many immune differences are reported and few replicate; genetics finds no risk enrichment in immune cells.
groups: Severe acute illness predicts who goes on to ME/CFS
No genetic enrichment in immune cells
Exhaustion features in CD8 T cells
Long COVID IgG transfers symptoms to mice
IgG subclass deficiency in a minority
Reduced TRPM3 current in NK cells

infection.takeaway: Infection is an established trigger; the evidence that a virus is still active is much weaker.
groups: About 1 in 10 meet criteria after EBV, Q fever or Ross River virus
New ME/CFS after COVID at 2.66 per 100 person-years
SARS-CoV-2 antigen persists in a minority
Standard herpesvirus serology does not differ

omics.takeaway: Blood chemistry differs at group level, but the effects are small and most single markers and classifiers do not replicate.

endocrine.takeaway: Cortisol is slightly low and the hormones that should restore blood volume fail to rise; hormone replacement has helped little.
groups: Renin and aldosterone not raised despite low volume
Adrenal and pituitary disease in a minority

gut.takeaway: Butyrate-producing bacteria are reduced and IBS is common, but genetics does not point to the gut as a cause.
groups: IBS about seven times more common
Overgrowth of R. gnavus and related species
Gut metabolites not causal by genetics

genetics.takeaway: Risk is heritable and polygenic, and the signal sits in neurons rather than immune cells.
groups: DecodeME signal replicates in other cohorts
Overlap with chronic pain, IBS and migraine

trials.takeaway: No treatment has a large, positive, placebo-controlled trial, and placebo response is large.

verdicts.vascular-endothelial: Reduced vessel dilation is replicated in Norwegian cohorts, but it is an average difference with wide overlap, and the antibody treatments aimed at its proposed cause have failed.
verdicts.small-vessel-capillary: Biopsy evidence for fewer or thickened capillaries is consistent but comes from small studies, mostly from one network, and no treatment aimed at it has a clean controlled result.
verdicts.low-blood-volume-preload: The physiology is among the best replicated in the field. What is missing is a sham-controlled trial showing that restoring volume or preload improves symptoms.
verdicts.autonomic-small-fibre: Autonomic abnormalities are common and replicated, but small-fibre neuropathy rates vary widely between centres, and treatments aimed at heart rate or autoimmune nerve damage have not helped.
verdicts.viral-persistence: Viral antigen persists in some people after COVID, but three antiviral trials in established long COVID were null, which argues against ongoing replication as the main driver.
verdicts.herpes-reactivation: Herpesviruses are clear triggers, but evidence of ongoing reactivation rests on antibody patterns that track replication poorly, and no antiviral trial has met its primary endpoint.
verdicts.autoimmunity: The leading antibody targets did not hold up and three antibody-targeting treatments failed controlled trials. Plasma-cell depletion and IgG-transfer results in mice keep a narrower version alive.
verdicts.immune-exhaustion: Exhaustion features in CD8 T cells are reported by more than one group, but immune-cell data give few signals that reproduce across cohorts.
verdicts.innate-hyperactivation: Cytokine findings in ME/CFS are small and poorly replicated, and steroid trials in long COVID did not help. Activation may be strongest early in the illness.
verdicts.complement-thromboinflammation: Replicated in long COVID, thin and inconsistent in ME/CFS. No complement inhibitor has been tested.
verdicts.microclots: The assay is not standardised, independent replication is lacking, and one large cohort found no difference from controls.
verdicts.cell-danger-response: A broad framework whose main metabolomic prediction, uniform hypometabolism, does not reproduce in later cohorts.
verdicts.mitochondrial-energy: Many signals point at energy metabolism, but most are early or contested, and the claim that patient serum impairs muscle mitochondria failed a pre-registered replication.
verdicts.metabolic-trap-ido: Genetics and Mendelian randomisation give it no support, and blood kynurenine data are inconsistent.
verdicts.hpa-endocrine: Mildly low cortisol is replicated, but it is small and nonspecific, and replacement gives little benefit, so it looks more like a consequence than a cause.
verdicts.pituitary-adh: Rests on one uncontrolled series. It is cheap to test properly with stimulated copeptin.
verdicts.neuroinflammation: PET evidence splits: positive in one small ME/CFS study and one long COVID study, negative in two others, one of which found the signal in muscle instead.
verdicts.brainstem-craniocervical: Case series only, from selected referral samples, and surgery carries real risk without a controlled trial.
verdicts.sickness-behaviour: Fits the symptoms and the post-infectious onset, but there is no direct evidence of persistent vagal signalling, and anti-inflammatory trials have been negative.
verdicts.gut-dysbiosis: Loss of butyrate producers is replicated, but Mendelian randomisation finds no causal effect of the gut metabolites tested, and dysbiosis fades with illness duration.
verdicts.genetic-neuronal: The DecodeME signal replicates and points at neurons. Individual loci and how they act are still unconfirmed.
verdicts.serum-factor: The cleanest test, patient serum on muscle cells, was null at n=120. IgG effects on endothelial cells and mice are newer and single-lab.
verdicts.sodium-calcium-overload: A coherent mechanism with little direct data: one 12-person sodium MRI study, and its proposed upstream antibody trigger has weakened.
verdicts.mast-cell: Observational support only, with inconsistent diagnostic criteria and no controlled trials.
verdicts.connective-tissue: Hypermobility is over-represented in clinic samples, but population data and a mechanism-specific test are lacking.
verdicts.integrated-hanson: The resting differences stand, but the main exercise-response claim weakens when each person is compared with their own baseline.
verdicts.omf-models: A bundle of separate ideas: the preload-failure strand is well supported, the nanoneedle and IDO strands are not.
verdicts.komaroff-lipkin-synthesis: Accurate as a catalogue of abnormalities, but broad enough to be hard to falsify.
verdicts.effort-preference: Based on 17 patients and an unvalidated task, and avoiding PEM explains the result equally well.
verdicts.cognitive-behavioural-model: Gains are confined to self-report and fade, and the model does not explain the objective abnormalities or the harm reported after graded exercise.
verdicts.deconditioning: Two-day exercise decline, preload failure and post-exertional muscle damage are not seen in sedentary controls, so lost fitness cannot be the whole explanation.
